subject: Immediate: Production 429s and timeout retry storm impacting HealthBridge
messages:
From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@healthbridge.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, contracts@healthbridge.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Immediate: Production 429s and timeouts impacting API throughput

Olga / Redwood team,

We're seeing a sudden, sustained spike of 429s and request timeouts across our production org starting ~16:10 PST. Error rate on POST /v1/generate spiked to ~32% and latency for successful requests jumped from 120ms to >1s. This started right after we rolled a small routing change on our side, but telemetry suggests calls are being rejected server-side with quota/limit responses.

Our customers are seeing failures in critical workflows and this is affecting our support SLAs. Can you triage immediately and confirm whether this is a Redwood-side quota/rate-limit issue vs something on our end?

Attached: hb_production_11-09-429.log (sample 10k lines), short telemetry CSV.

Urgent asks:
- Confirm whether any org/project limits were changed or pushed today on your platform
- Immediate mitigation steps we can take to restore throughput
- ETA for a fix and whether you can temporarily relax limits for our org

Thanks,
Daniel Cho
Technical Ops Lead, HealthBridge
Daniel.Cho@healthbridge.com
Attachment: hb_production_11-09-429.log (text), healthbridge-mup-telemetry.csv (csv)
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@healthbridge.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Hi Daniel — thanks for the quick heads-up and logs. I'm escalating to SRE/serving immediately (cc'd). We treat 5xx/429 spikes as Sev-2 when customer-facing degradation is happening.

We're starting a phone bridge now; I need two quick clarifications while Marcus/Rishi investigate:
- Is the traffic burst across multiple projects under your org or tied to a single project ID?
- Can you confirm if you recently changed API keys, routing prefixes, or project labels in the last 2 hours?

Immediate next steps from us:
- Marcus/Rishi will validate quota/tiering assignments and routing policies for your org/projects
- If we detect a mapping misassignment we will perform an emergency quota override to restore throughput (short-lived)
- We'll provide a mutual action plan and ETA within 60 minutes

We have a JIRA ticket started (RINF-6821) and I'm marking this high priority.

—Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 18:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Immediate: Production 429s and timeouts impacting API throughput

Olga / team — quick findings from initial triage:
- Observed behavior: Large number of retries (~2.8k req/s) from HealthBridge org caused a feedback amplification when requests started hitting project-level quota (project: hb-prod-01). Many clients retried aggressively (exponential backoff not respected) causing a retry storm.
- Root cause signal: A recent tenant labeling change during an internal routing rollout caused HealthBridge traffic to be assigned the default project quota instead of the reserved project quota (org-level quota vs project-level allocation mismatch). The project-level cap is ~3.5 rps sustained per token bucket which HealthBridge exceeded, triggering 429s.
- Complicating factor: Tiering policy mismatch — the fallback variant for their org is on a stricter rate plan because the org id was mis-tagged as a trial tier in the mapping table.

Immediate mitigations we executed (18:00 PST):
1) Apply emergency override to increase project hb-prod-01 quota to a safe temporary level (bumped to 150 rps) — this restored success rate to ~98% within ~3 minutes.
2) Placed a short client-side backoff advisement in the gateway to reduce retry fan-out for 5 minutes.
3) Rotated rate-mapping table to correct the label assignment that had been flipped during the routing rollout. Snapshot attached: quota-mapping-annot.png

Next actions (owner / ETA):
- Rishi: Merge permanent fix to routing/tiering mapping and validate across staging & prod (ETA: 24h)
- Marcus: Follow up to confirm derived cost/impact for the temporary override and propose credit (ETA: 48h)
- Olga: Customer communications & exec ping (ongoing)

I'll keep the JIRA updated; adding logs to the ticket.

Attachment: quota-mapping-annot.png (annotated mapping snapshot)

—Marcus Lin
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@healthbridge.com>

Olga / Marcus,

Thanks for the rapid response and for bumping the quota — we can confirm error rates are back down and throughput is much improved. Appreciate the emergency override.

Two asks from our side:
- We need a short incident summary we can share internally (what happened, why, and when it was resolved) for our on-call postmortem.
- HealthBridge requests a bill/credit review for the production impact window (11/09 16:10–18:05 PST). Our finance team CC'd contracts for follow-up.

Also: please advise any configuration changes we should avoid while you complete the permanent fix.

—Daniel
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@healthbridge.com>, marcus_lin@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Post-incident summary and next steps — HealthBridge 429 spike (RINF-6821)

Team / Daniel — final summary and action items (concise):

Summary (what happened)
- Timeline: 2026-11-09 16:10 PST — spike began; 18:00 PST — emergency override applied; 18:05 PST — success rate recovered.
- Root cause: Routing/tiering mapping regression during an internal rollout caused HealthBridge’s traffic to be assigned a stricter project quota and trial-tier fallback. When normal traffic patterns continued, their clients retried aggressively after 429s, producing a retry storm and amplification of errors.
- Impact: Elevated 429 rate and timeouts for HealthBridge production endpoints, customer-visible failures for approximately 2 hours.

Actions taken
- Emergency override to increase hb-prod-01 quota (temporary) and short gateway backoff guidance (done at 18:00 PST)
- Corrected mapping table and rolled the permanent mapping fix to staging (Rishi)
- Added additional telemetry alerts to detect sudden org->project assignment changes (Marcus)
- Created runbook update to require a mapping sanity-check before routing rollouts (owner: Product/ServOps)

Follow-ups / Ownership
- Rishi Malhotra: deploy mapping fix to prod, add unit/integration checks (ETA: 24h)
- Marcus Lin: cost analysis and proposed credit; will propose amount and submit to finance/vendor credits (ETA: 48h)
- Olga Petrov: customer-facing incident summary & exec update; coordinate HubSpot ticket and finance (ongoing)

Links/Artifacts
- JIRA: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RINF-6821
- Logs: hb_production_11-09-429.log (attached); telemetry CSV attached
- Runbook: https://internal.redwood.com/runbooks/quota-mapping

HealthBridge finance / contracts — Olga will loop legal/finance to process a goodwill credit for the impacted window; Marcus will provide a cost assessment and recommended credit.

Apologies again for the disruption. We are treating this as a priority change to our rollout checklist so this does not recur. I will update the thread when Rishi's prod fix is live.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: hb_production_11-09-429.log, healthbridge-mup-telemetry.csv
